proof.text:
Unpack the enriched-end mapping sets specified in [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], using only their definition, not its model-structure existence assertion. For an $n$-simplex $u$ of $B(b,b')$, the map $H_j(u)$ is an $n$-simplex of the enriched end, with evaluation $H_j(u)_i$ and enriched naturality in $i$. For an $n$-simplex $v$ of $I(i,i')$, set
$$e_j(u,v)=H_j(b')(v)\circ H_j(u)_i=H_j(u)_{i'}\circ H_j(b)(v).$$
The equality is the end's enriched naturality equation. Both expressions commute with simplicial operators. For composable pairs $(u,v),(u',v')$, move $H_j(u')_{i'}$ past $H_j(b')(v)$ by that equation; associativity and functoriality give $e_j(u',v')e_j(u,v)=e_j(u'u,v'v)$. Identity pairs map to identities. Thus this formula defines the enriched functor $e_j$ on $B\times I$. All its objects are bifibrant by hypothesis, so its target is the full simplicial subcategory $\mathcal A^{cf}$. No cofibrancy condition on diagrams is used.

source.place: Section 1.1.5, Definition 1.1.5.5 and Example 1.1.5.8; explicit enriched evaluation and interval construction (agent argument).

proof.text:
Put $D=B\times I$ and $r_{(b,i)}=q_b(i)$. Naturality of the enriched transformation $q$ in $B$ gives $q_{b'}(i)H_0(u)_i=H_1(u)_i q_b(i)$ as an equality on the entire mapping simplicial set. Since $q_{b'}$ is an enriched transformation of $I$-diagrams, $q_{b'}(i')H_0(b')(v)=H_1(b')(v)q_{b'}(i)$. Substituting these two equalities into step 1 gives
$$r_{(b',i')}e_0(u,v)=e_1(u,v)r_{(b,i)}.$$
Here vertices are made constant $n$-simplices when composed with $n$-simplices. Consequently these equalities hold as simplicial maps, not merely for arrows of an underlying ordinary category. They prove enriched naturality of $r:e_0\Rightarrow e_1$.

source.place: Section 1.1.5, Definition 1.1.5.5 and Example 1.1.5.8; explicit enriched evaluation and interval construction (agent argument).

proof.text:
Construct $J:D\times[1]\to\mathcal A^{cf}$ explicitly. On objects put $J(x,\epsilon)=e_\epsilon(x)$. On a mapping object with endpoints both $0$ or both $1$, use $e_0$ or $e_1$, respectively. On the cross mapping object from $(x,0)$ to $(y,1)$ put
$$J(f,0\to1)=r_y e_0(f)=e_1(f)r_x.$$
On the empty mapping object from level $1$ to level $0$ use its unique map. This defines simplicial maps by step 2. Composable interval arrows have levels $000,001,011,111$. The constant cases use the functor laws of $e_j$. For $001$ the composite is $r_z e_0(g)e_0(f)=r_z e_0(gf)$; for $011$ it is $e_1(g)r_y e_0(f)=r_z e_0(g)e_0(f)=r_z e_0(gf)$, by step 2. Identities at both levels are preserved. This verifies every enriched functor law, and the image of $(1_x,0\to1)$ is exactly $r_x$.

source.place: Section 1.1.5, Definition 1.1.5.5 and Example 1.1.5.8; explicit enriched evaluation and interval construction (agent argument).

proof.text:
Write $Q=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal A^{cf})$ and $X=N_{\mathrm{hc}}B$. The first is a quasicategory by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], and the second is one by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], since $B$ is locally Kan. Directly from the nerve formula in that comparison, a functor from $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ to a product is a pair of functors. These degreewise bijections commute with simplex operators. Hence the coherent nerve preserves the products in question. Its value on the discrete simplicial category $[1]$ is its ordinary nerve, $\Delta^1$, by the same cited statement. Taking the nerve of $J$ and precomposing by $1_X\times a\times1_{\Delta^1}$ therefore gives
$$X\times K\times\Delta^1\longrightarrow Q.$$
Reorder the last two factors and apply [lem-coef-joyal-strict-currying]. The result $X\times\Delta^1\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$ is an edge $\eta:E_0\to E_1$ of the outer functor simplicial set. Restriction to the endpoints agrees with the definition of $E_j$. Restriction to $(b,k)\times\Delta^1$ is the nerve edge of $r_{(b,a(k))}=q_b(a(k))$, because step 3 sends the interval arrow at that object to this vertex.

source.place: Section 1.1.5, Definition 1.1.5.5 and Example 1.1.5.8; explicit enriched evaluation and interval construction (agent argument).

proof.text: For each $(b,i)$, the arrow $q_b(i)$ is a weak equivalence between bifibrant objects. Under the inverse equivalence from $Q$ to the infinity localization in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], its nerve edge maps to this arrow followed by localization; the agreement with inclusion on bifibrant objects is part of that node's statement. Localization inverts this arrow. An equivalence of categories reflects invertibility: apply its quasi-inverse to an inverse and the two inverse-triangle witnesses, then conjugate by the comparison equivalences with the identity. Thus the original edge of $Q$ is an equivalence. In particular every edge computed at the end of step 4 is an equivalence.

source.place: Section 1.1.5, Definition 1.1.5.5 and Example 1.1.5.8; explicit enriched evaluation and interval construction (agent argument).

proof.text: Set $R=\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$. For completeness, $R$ is a quasicategory: by [lem-coef-joyal-strict-currying], a horn in $R$ is a map $K\times\Lambda_i^n\to Q$. The map $\Lambda_i^n\times K\to\Delta^n\times K$ is inner anodyne by [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product], applied to the inner horn and $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$. Since $Q\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration by the definition of quasicategory, the required extension exists. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] first with target $Q$ and index $K$: for each vertex $b$ of $X$, the edge $\eta_b$ in $R$ is an equivalence, since its components at all $k$ are the equivalences of step 5. Apply that same node again, now with target $R$ and index $X$, to conclude that $\eta$ is an equivalence edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(X,R)$. This is the asserted coherent natural equivalence, induced by precisely the interval functor of step 3. These arguments also cover empty $K$, $I$, or $B$: the corresponding vertex conditions are vacuous.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.4.4; apply twice, after the explicit inner-horn lifting argument for the internal functor simplicial set.

title: Coherence of enriched evaluation with projective replacement
statement:
Use simplicial model categories and the homotopy coherent nerve $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], small simplicial categories of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and coherent functor categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a simplicial model category, let $I$ be a small simplicial category, let $B$ be a locally Kan simplicial category (all its mapping simplicial sets are Kan), and let $H_0,H_1:B\to\operatorname{Fun}_{\Delta}(I,\mathcal A)$ be simplicial functors. The target is the simplicial category of enriched functors with the enriched-end mapping simplicial sets as in [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]; no model structure on it is required. Assume every value $H_j(b)(i)$ is bifibrant. Let $q:H_0\Rightarrow H_1$ be a simplicially enriched natural transformation, meaning component vertices whose naturality equations hold as equalities of simplicial maps on all mapping objects, and assume every component $q_b(i)$ is a weak equivalence in $\mathcal A$. Fix a small simplicial set $K$ and any map $a:K\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}I$. Universes may be enlarged to contain $B$ and $\mathcal A$.

Enriched evaluation defines functors $e_j:B\times I\to\mathcal A^{cf}$ by $e_j(b,i)=H_j(b)(i)$. Take their coherent nerves, using $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(B\times I)=N_{\mathrm{hc}}B\times N_{\mathrm{hc}}I$, precompose in the second variable with $a$, and curry to obtain
$$E_j:N_{\mathrm{hc}}B\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(K,N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal A^{cf})).$$
There is a coherent natural equivalence $E_0\Rightarrow E_1$ induced by enriched evaluation of $q$. Its component at $(b,k)$ is the edge corresponding to $q_b(a(k))$. More precisely, the enriched transformation $e_0\Rightarrow e_1$ with components $q_b(i)$ defines a simplicial functor $(B\times I)\times[1]\to\mathcal A^{cf}$, where $[1]$ has discrete mapping sets; its nerve, precomposed with $a$ and curried, is this natural equivalence. Here $a(k)$ denotes the object of $I$ corresponding to the vertex $a(k)$ of its nerve. No assumption that either $E_j$ is an equivalence is made.
